head_commit.message:
Landing: photo matches shot inside the live scene, best-verdict pairs, and the hero "g" (#1619)

* Landing: a new front door that leads with 4D Chicago and its films

The chicago.polecat.live home page was a four-card list. It is now a
cinematic front door for the project, 4D first:

- Hero: a 1280x720 loop filmed in the app (1812 up to the stockade, the
  1835 town and wharves, Prairie Avenue and the lakefront in 1904) behind
  "Walk Chicago as the record describes it", with Enter 4D Chicago, the
  1:20 film, and straight links to /4d/1812/, /4d/1835/, /4d/1904/.
- Three summers: one large row per year — Fort Dearborn (0:49), the river
  town (0:58), Prairie Avenue (0:51) — each with its scene date, a Watch
  button and a Walk-it link. The 1835 row carries a short, factual note on
  the August 1835 Potawatomi removal and why the 1 July scene does not
  stage it (AGENTS.md, standing constraint).
- The record: attested / inferred / reconstructed explained beside three
  real screens from the app (Glessner House's record with its c. 1889
  photograph, the Sauganash over the confidence view, the 1812 barracks
  graded 4 / 6 / 4).
- Prairie Avenue: a full-bleed feature with the library's own counts
  (62 buildings, 138 sources, 38 maps from prairie-1904/data/library.json)
  linking to the library and to /4d/1904/.
- The atlas: a 1674-1911 coverage timeline and cards for Before the Fire,
  Chicago Rebuilds and Prairie Avenue (record and map counts unchanged).
- One player for all four films, switchable in place; films load only
  when opened, the hero plays only on screen, and never under reduced
  motion or Save-Data.

Footage was filmed frame by frame from the dev build through the app's
own window.__chicago4d camera API (as tools/portal_clips.mjs does), at
dev@34dd87e2. The notes widget (data-page="home") and the chicago.theme
key are kept. site/css/site.css is left in place, unused by this page.
The landing is main-only per chicago/4d/docs/PIPELINE.md section 4.

* Landing: newest first — Prairie Avenue 1904, then 1835, then 1812

The owner asked for the page to run in reverse and feature Prairie
Avenue first.

- The Prairie Avenue feature now sits directly under the hero.
- Film rows run 1904 → 1835 → 1812; hero year links, hero copy, the
  player's tabs, the footer and the meta descriptions follow suit.
- The hero loop is re-cut to open on Prairie Avenue (up the avenue, the
  lakefront) before the 1835 wharves and town and the 1812 stockade.
- The combined film is re-cut newest first (1:24): "Three summers." →
  Prairie Avenue (now with its arrival screen and Glessner House's
  record) → "1835 · Sixty-nine years earlier" → "1812 · Twenty-three
  years earlier" → end card. Replaced files carry ?v=2.
- The atlas timeline stays chronological — it is an axis.

* Landing: photo-matched pairs, an animated "how it's made" flow, and a contact page

- Photo-matched (new section after the films): eight archive-and-model
  pairs from chicago/4d/docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/, each the archival
  picture beside the model rendered from that picture's fitted camera,
  filterable by year — Glessner House, the Kimball house and the Pullman
  house (1904); St. Mary's, the Green Tree Inn and the Dearborn Street
  drawbridge (1835); the Kinzie house and Lee's Place (1812). Every
  archival half is public domain or carries no known restrictions in its
  data/sources record (HABS / Library of Congress, Art Institute Taylor
  print, Andreas 1884, Chicago Magazine 1857, Currey 1912), and is
  credited on the card.
- How it's made (new section near the bottom): Gather -> Read & place ->
  Match & grade -> Build -> Walk, each naming the real sources and tools
  (Thompson 1830, Rees & Rucker 1849, Robinson 1886, Sanborn 1911; the
  1830/1840/1900 manuscript censuses; directories 1839-1911; camera
  solve; bpy in a pinned Blender -> glTF + KTX2 + JSON sidecars ->
  three.js). Packets carrying source thumbnails travel the wire and
  relabel at each stage; each stage cross-fades real pictures (the
  Sanborn sheet and Robinson plate already published in prairie-1904/).
  Reduced motion shows it static.
- Contact: /contact/ posts to FormSubmit (AJAX, honeypot, mailto
  fallback; works without JS via _next), delivering to the project's
  address; the home page closes on a "Bring us a place" call to action.

* Landing: a research library linking the reference corpus on GitHub

A new "Read the sources yourself" section (#reference, after the atlas;
"Research" in the nav, two links in the footer) with 20 verified links in
four groups:

- Images & maps: chicago/reference/images (72 catalogued views) and
  IMAGE_SOURCES.md, the Prairie Avenue Sanborn 1911 / Robinson 1886
  sheets, the photo-match studies (53 structures) and their fitted
  cameras (data/reference_views).
- People & records: the 1840 census readings and name crosswalk,
  resident research, the Chicago Democrat 1833-1835 and Chicago American
  with transcriptions, the St. Mary's baptisms 1833-1835, Wau-Bun.
- Sources & studies: data/sources (515 records), docs/RESEARCH,
  PROVENANCE.md, LIBERTIES.md, and the atlas datasets.
- Internet Archive: the chicago1835-* deposits (Andreas, the Chicago
  Democrat 1835, the Chicago American, the Fergus series, and the full
  chicago1835 search).

Plus "Browse /reference" and the corpus manifest up top. Every URL
returned 200 when checked.

* Landing: photo matches shot inside the live scene, best-verdict pairs, and the hero "g"

The owner asked for better matches than the Kimball house (its match
record reads "differs", 30 open differences) and for the model to be
shown in its surroundings rather than alone on a grey plane.

- Every 4D image is now rendered inside the live dev app (chicago.polecat.live/4d/dev/)
  from the reference view's own camera: data/reference_views/<id>/<view>.json's
  focal length, principal point (view offset), basis or yaw, pixel aspect and
  footprint-frame eye, carried into world coordinates through the structure's
  scene placement (local_e/local_n/rotation_deg, as tools/photo_match_group.mjs
  defines the frame) and the app's own ground height. Streets, neighbours,
  enclosures, furniture and terrain come with it; trees and flora are switched
  off because, in the app's summer, they hid the buildings.
- Six pairs, chosen by the match records' verdicts and image rights:
  1904 — Glessner House from the north-east (Taylor 2135, AIC, matches),
  the Keith house (Inland Architect Feb. 1888, cleared, matches), First
  Presbyterian Church (Otis 1913 plate of 1887, matches); 1835 — the
  Sauganash Hotel with Philo Carpenter's shop (Andreas 1884; close, 4 open
  differences), the Miller house at Wolf Point (Blanchard/Shober 1867,
  NYPL, matches); 1812 — the Kinzie house (Chicago Magazine 1857; close,
  8 open differences). Each card shows that verdict.
- Pairs keep their photograph's own aspect ratio.
- Hero: the headline's line mask clipped the "g" of Chicago; its bottom
  padding now clears descenders, with a matching negative margin so the
  spacing is unchanged.
